payload.statement:
Fix \(p\in\mathfrak O\) and a finite family \(\mathcal A_p\) of real matrices.  Let
\[
X_m=m^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^m(\mathbf e_{O_i}-p),
\qquad G_p\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_p),
\]
where the \(O_i\) in this display are an independent size-\(m\) sample from \(p\).  For \(M\in\mathcal A_p\), set
\[
\Omega_M=M\Sigma_pM^{\top},\qquad r_M=\operatorname{rank}(\Omega_M),
\]
and define
\[
\delta_m(p)=\max_{M\in\mathcal A_p}\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(M)}}
\left|\Pr_p\{MX_m\leq x\}-\Pr\{MG_p\leq x\}\right|.
\]
With the maximum over an empty set interpreted as zero, put
\[
C(p)=\max\left\{0,\max_{M\in\mathcal A_p:r_M>0}
\left(42r_M^{1/4}+16\right)
\sum_{o\in\mathcal O}p_o
\left\|\Omega_M^{\dagger/2}M(\mathbf e_o-p)\right\|_2^3\right\}.
\]
Then \(C(p)<\infty\) for fixed \(p\) and
\[
\delta_m(p)\leq C(p)m^{-1/2}.
\]
This assertion restricts and whitens on \(\operatorname{range}(\Omega_M)\); it does not apply an identity-covariance theorem directly to a singular \(\Omega_M\).  The constant is pointwise and need not be uniform as covariance ranks degenerate.  Moreover, for
\[
m_n=\max\{1,\lfloor n^{1/3}\rfloor\},
\qquad
\eta_n=\min\{\alpha/2,n^{-1/12}\},
\]
one has
\[
\delta_{m_n}(p)=O(n^{-1/6}),\qquad
\frac{m_n}{\sqrt n}=O(n^{-1/6}),\qquad
\frac{m_n^2}{n}=O(n^{-1/3}),
\]
and, for every fixed \(c>0\), \(e^{-cm_n}=O(e^{-c'n^{1/3}})\) for some \(c'>0\); every displayed term is \(o(\eta_n)\).
payload.proof_tex:
Fix \(M\in\mathcal A_p\) and abbreviate \(\Omega=\Omega_M\) and \(r=r_M\).  The categorical summand \(W=M(\mathbf e_{O_1}-p)\) is centered and satisfies
\[
\mathbb E_p[WW^{\top}]=M\{\operatorname{diag}(p)-pp^{\top}\}M^{\top}=\Omega.
\tag{1}
\]
If \(r=0\), then \(\Omega=0\), because it is positive semidefinite, and
\[
\mathbb E_p\|W\|_2^2=\operatorname{tr}(\Omega)=0.
\]
Thus \(W=0\) almost surely.  The centered Gaussian vector \(MG_p\) also has covariance zero and is zero almost surely, so the lower-orthant approximation error for this \(M\) equals zero.

Suppose \(r>0\).  Choose a matrix \(Q\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(M)\times r}\) whose columns form an orthonormal basis of \(\operatorname{range}(\Omega)\), and set
\[
\overline\Omega=Q^{\top}\Omega Q.
\]
The matrix \(\overline\Omega\) is positive definite: if \(u\neq0\), then \(Qu\) is a nonzero vector in \(\operatorname{range}(\Omega)\), which is orthogonal to \(\ker(\Omega)\), and hence
\[
u^{\top}\overline\Omega u=(Qu)^{\top}\Omega(Qu)>0.
\tag{2}
\]
For the independent categorical observations define
\[
\xi_i=m^{-1/2}\overline\Omega^{-1/2}Q^{\top}M(\mathbf e_{O_i}-p),
\qquad i=1,\ldots,m.
\]
Equations (1)--(2) give
\[
\mathbb E_p\xi_i=0,
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^m\mathbb E_p[\xi_i\xi_i^{\top}]
=\overline\Omega^{-1/2}Q^{\top}\Omega Q\overline\Omega^{-1/2}=I_r.
\tag{3}
\]

If \(a\in\ker(\Omega)\), then \(\mathbb E_p(a^{\top}W)^2=a^{\top}\Omega a=0\), so \(a^{\top}W=0\) almost surely.  Therefore both \(MX_m\) and \(MG_p\) lie in \(\operatorname{range}(\Omega)\) almost surely.  For every lower orthant \(( -\infty,x]\) in the original row space, its inverse image under the injective linear map
\[
u\longmapsto Q\overline\Omega^{1/2}u
\]
is the convex set
\[
K_x=\{u\in\mathbb R^r:Q\overline\Omega^{1/2}u\leq x\}.
\tag{4}
\]
Applying \(\text{lem:raic-multivariate-berry-esseen-convex-sets}\) to (3) and (4) gives
\[
\sup_x\left|\Pr_p\{MX_m\leq x\}-\Pr\{MG_p\leq x\}\right|
\leq(42r^{1/4}+16)\sum_{i=1}^m\mathbb E_p\|\xi_i\|_2^3.
\tag{5}
\]
Because the \(m\) summands are identically distributed and carry the factor \(m^{-1/2}\),
\[
\sum_{i=1}^m\mathbb E_p\|\xi_i\|_2^3
=m^{-1/2}\sum_{o\in\mathcal O}p_o
\left\|\overline\Omega^{-1/2}Q^{\top}M(\mathbf e_o-p)\right\|_2^3.
\tag{6}
\]
On \(\operatorname{range}(\Omega)\), the Moore--Penrose inverse square root is
\[
\Omega^{\dagger/2}=Q\overline\Omega^{-1/2}Q^{\top}.
\]
Since \(M(\mathbf e_o-p)\in\operatorname{range}(\Omega)\) for every \(o\) with \(p_o>0\), and since \(Q\) is an isometry, the norm in (6) equals
\[
\left\|\Omega^{\dagger/2}M(\mathbf e_o-p)\right\|_2.
\tag{7}
\]
Equations (5)--(7), followed by the maximum over the finite family \(\mathcal A_p\), prove
\[
\delta_m(p)\leq C(p)m^{-1/2}.
\tag{8}
\]
Every term defining \(C(p)\) is finite for a fixed finite matrix and a fixed \(p\), and \(\mathcal A_p\) is finite, so \(C(p)<\infty\).  This argument also displays why the conclusion is not uniform near a covariance-rank change: the nonzero eigenvalues inverted in \(\Omega^{\dagger/2}\) may approach zero.

It remains to verify the announced schedule.  For all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\tfrac12n^{1/3}\leq m_n\leq n^{1/3},
\qquad
\eta_n=n^{-1/12}.
\]
Consequently (8) and elementary exponent arithmetic yield
\[
\delta_{m_n}(p)=O(n^{-1/6}),\qquad
m_n/\sqrt n=O(n^{-1/6}),\qquad
m_n^2/n=O(n^{-1/3}).
\tag{9}
\]
After division by \(\eta_n=n^{-1/12}\), the three orders in (9) become respectively \(O(n^{-1/12})\), \(O(n^{-1/12})\), and \(O(n^{-1/4})\), all tending to zero.  Finally, \(m_n\geq n^{1/3}/2\) eventually, so
\[
e^{-cm_n}\leq e^{-(c/2)n^{1/3}}=o(n^{-1/12})=o(\eta_n).
\]
This proves every claimed comparison.

payload.partial_result:
The fixed-law approximation component is complete: \(\text{lem:finite-alphabet-fan-berry-esseen-explicit-schedule}\) proves \(\delta_m(p)\leq C(p)m^{-1/2}\) by effective-range whitening and gives \(m_n=\max\{1,\lfloor n^{1/3}\rfloor\}\), \(\eta_n=\min\{\alpha/2,n^{-1/12}\}\), with every coupling, collision, Berry--Esseen, and exponential localization error \(o(\eta_n)\).  The generic global-sign subsampling argument in the prior partial progress then proves the advertised pointwise conditional quantile inequality under the fixed finite-fan and Gaussian-nondegeneracy hypotheses.

For the thirty-two-type early-kill instance, the complete table gives \(b_{13}=b_{29}=\tfrac12(\mathbf e_2+\mathbf e_8)\) and \(b_{30}=\tfrac12(\mathbf e_2+\mathbf e_{12})\).  Put \(d_i=b_i-p_\dagger\).  The directed vector
\[
z_1=d_3+d_4+d_{13}+d_{14}
=\tfrac12(-3\mathbf e_7+\mathbf e_8+\mathbf e_9+\mathbf e_{11})
\]
is tangent, and the directed lower and upper type-weight directions both have zero mass, incidence image \(z_1\), and objectives two and zero, respectively.  Nevertheless it is not the Euclidean tangent-cone projection of \(g_1=\mathbf e_2+\mathbf e_3-2\mathbf e_7\).  Its residual is
\[
r_1=g_1-z_1
=\mathbf e_2+\mathbf e_3-\tfrac12(\mathbf e_7+\mathbf e_8+\mathbf e_9+\mathbf e_{11}),
\]
and exact multiplication gives
\[
r_1^{\top}p_\dagger=\tfrac14,\qquad
r_1^{\top}b_{30}=\tfrac12,\qquad
r_1^{\top}d_{30}
=r_1^{\top}(b_{30}-p_\dagger)=\tfrac14>0.
\]
Thus \(r_1\notin T_{\mathfrak O^{32}}(p_\dagger)^\circ\), violating the necessary Moreau polar condition.  Independently, \(d_{13}=d_{29}\), so their polar products must agree, while the directed vector lists them as zero and \(-1/2\).  The zero-direction projection and zero cone remain valid, but exact multiplication gives its polar products at columns \(29,30,31,32\) as \((-2,-2,-8/5,-8/5)\), not four copies of \(-8/5\).  The lower certificate \(\lambda^A\) has slack \(-1\) at columns \(29,30\), whereas the upper certificate \(\lambda^B\) has slack \(+1\) there.  Hence both the directed positive-projection list and the directed last-four zero-projection list contain exact mismatches.  In particular, the proposed positive-direction projection cannot support \(D_L(g_1)=2\), and the required nondegenerate-atom certificate remains the sole unresolved part of the target.

payload.tldr: Repeated trials cannot accompany every updated human--AI policy, and pretrial ground truth is revealed only by an endogenous action. The headline result is the arbitrary-finite-SLCC dual-face necessary-and-sufficient characterization of when retained labels strictly improve each sharp endpoint, together with the primitive bracket-stratum family proving that a nonempty relatively open two-sided strict-refinement region exists. The possibly noninjective and nonminimal thirty-two-row quotient-generating cover is an exact witness and implementation corollary: it gives \([1/2,3/4]\) versus the label-blind \([1/4,1]\), and \([397/800,601/800]\) versus \([99/400,1]\) at a relative-interior perturbation. Simultaneous multinomial confidence-region propagation gives finite-sample whole-set coverage, and Euclidean projection gives the projection-composed directional limit. Effective-range whitening now yields the explicit fixed-law rate and schedules for the centered atomic-tie argument, but the requested thirty-two-type nondegenerate-atom instantiation remains uncertified because its directed positive projection fails an exact polar inequality.

project_justification.fill: The project first gives the computable dual-face if-and-only-if tests for arbitrary finite SLCC incidence models and then uses the primitive bracket-stratum condition to construct a stable relative-interior two-sided strict-refinement region. The noninjective and nonminimal thirty-two-row cover supplies an exact rational witness and implementation fixture rather than the sole novelty kernel. The finite-response converse makes both LP endpoints sharp, simultaneous multinomial confidence propagation gives whole-set coverage, and the rank-adaptive Berry--Esseen argument supplies explicit fixed-law subsample and slack schedules. The final advertised nondegenerate atomic-tie certificate is not yet accepted because the currently directed positive projection violates an exact tangent-polar condition.

payload.related_work: Zhang, Skalnes, Chen, and Oberst (2026, Assumptions 3.1--3.3, Theorem 4.1, the Tightness of Bounds discussion, Theorem 5.1, and Appendix G) supply the correctness, performance-order, and neutral restrictions, but do not claim their main bounds are tight and do not treat the present endogenous reveal action. Chen and Oberst (2025, Theorems 3.1--3.2) prove attained bounds in the preceding performance-mediated model without the selective-label correctness quotient. Lakkaraju et al. (2017, p. 4, Proposition 4.1) formalize decision-induced labels through contraction across decision makers rather than a sharp compatible-SCM fiber. Imai et al. (2023) supply the randomized PSA consumer, while Ben-Michael et al. (2025, Theorem 3 and Theorem S3) analyze classification-risk contrasts under a different baseline-potential-outcome design. Duarte et al. (2024, Proposition 1 and Theorem 1) provide the general finite response-function optimization framework, and Section 6 with Appendix E gives generic propagation of simultaneous observable-law confidence regions. The present identification contribution leads with the full-versus-blind optimal-dual-face equivalence for every finite SLCC design and the primitive bracket-stratum family producing a nonempty relatively open strict region; the thirty-two-row cover is its exact witness and corollary. Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) provide the calibrated-projection benchmark. Fang and Santos (2019, Theorem 2.1 and Section 4) provide the directional delta method and convex-projection derivative, while the paired LP optimal-face composition is specialized here. Rai\v{c} (2019, Theorem 1.1) gives the identity-covariance convex-set Berry--Esseen inequality; the note's effective-range whitening adapts it to singular fan matrices and yields the fixed \(n^{1/3}\) subsample and \(n^{-1/12}\) slack schedules. Hong and Li (2018) provide a numerical derivative alternative. Andrews and Han (2009) show that \(m/n\to0\) alone does not justify centered endpoint subsampling. The generic fixed-law global-sign argument closes with the explicit rate, but the current thirty-two-type nondegenerate-atom certificate remains open after its proposed projection failed exact verification.
payload.interpretation: For a fitted finite SLCC model, an analyst solves the two full endpoint LPs. Retained labels improve the lower endpoint exactly when no full lower-optimal dual certificate is representable using only label-blind rows, with the analogous criterion for the upper endpoint. These are finite feasibility checks. The bracket-stratum condition guarantees that both checks succeed on a stable set of relative-interior laws, while the thirty-two-row cover supplies exact rational regression fixtures for the Imai PSA and aihuman workflows. At a fixed boundary law, the effective-range constant makes the subsample and slack schedules explicit; an exact tangent-polar and primal-dual audit is still required before using the proposed nondegenerate atomic-tie witness.
payload.technical_internal_limitation: The full-model sharpness and strict-refinement results include legal realization and actual relative interior. The fixed-law Berry--Esseen constant and generic global-sign subsampling proof are pointwise and nonuniform near covariance-rank changes. The currently directed thirty-two-type positive projection is not polar-feasible, so the promised nondegenerate atomic-tie instantiation and hence the complete strengthened theorem remain open. Even after that certificate is repaired, uniform-in-law coverage, data-dependent fan selection, and finite-sample optimal tuning are outside the present result.
payload.honest_scope: The identification results concern finite strata and policies, three distinct certified performance levels in the strictness witness, and binary actions, labels, and outcomes. Certified performance values are external inputs. Generic confidence-region propagation supplies finite-sample whole-set coverage. The general dual-face characterization and primitive bracket family are the headline; the possibly noninjective and nonminimal thirty-two-row cover is their witness and corollary. The projection-composed limit is pointwise. Effective-range whitening proves a fixed-law \(m^{-1/2}\) approximation rate and the explicit choices \(m_n=\max\{1,\lfloor n^{1/3}\rfloor\}\) and \(\eta_n=\min\{\alpha/2,n^{-1/12}\}\), but the requested exact thirty-two-type nondegenerate-atom certificate has not passed its polar check. Uniform-in-law validity, data-dependent fan selection, finite-sample optimal tuning, multiclass actions, dynamic policies, violation budgets, joint deployment targets, and policy learning remain outside this kernel. Equality of the untrialed and a trialed configuration recovers the randomized observed mean, while full revelation of \(Z\) removes masking but does not identify a distinct untrialed configuration. Sharpness is not claimed to transfer to Zhang et al.'s incompatible published observation model.
